evidence: channelz/service/service_test.go:272-274 defines a v1-only message with Reset, String and ProtoMessage methods.
reflection/grpc_testing_not_regenerate/testv3.go:288-291 defines Reset, String, ProtoMessage, and Descriptor on SearchRequestV3 but no ProtoReflect; line 333 passes it to grpc.Invoke.
The base codec asserted github.com/golang/protobuf/proto.Message, whose v1 interface accepts these messages.

The new proto.Message requires ProtoReflect while the previous github.com/golang/protobuf/proto.Message accepts Reset, String, and ProtoMessage. For example, channelz/service/service_test.go:267-274 defines a legacy message with only those methods.
encoding/proto/proto.go:49 performs the same assertion on incoming messages; a rejected message returns an error before serialization or deserialization.
provenance: da3facf0f Clement 2023-10-18 - imported the new proto package in the reviewed range.
findings.suggested_fix: Accept both protoadapt.MessageV1 and protoadapt.MessageV2 in Marshal and Unmarshal, converting v1 messages using protoadapt.MessageV2Of before invoking the new protobuf API; add a legacy-message round trip test.
findings.title: Preserve support for legacy protobuf messages in the codec
findings.why_it_matters: RPCs using messages generated by the original protobuf generator now fail during marshaling or unmarshaling because those messages implement the v1 interface but not ProtoReflect. The repository's SearchRequestV3 is one concrete example and is passed to grpc.Invoke. Accepting v1 messages and adapting them to v2 before marshaling and unmarshaling preserves existing clients and servers.

evidence: The previous ptypes.DynamicAny path uses ptypes.Empty, which calls proto.MessageV1 on the registered message; protoadapt.MessageV1Of performs the equivalent unwrapping.
github.com/golang/protobuf@v1.5.3/ptypes/any.go:77 returns proto.MessageV1(mt.New().Interface()) for DynamicAny; protoadapt.MessageV1Of unwraps v1 messages.
findings.suggested_fix: Append protoadapt.MessageV1Of(detail) so v1-only messages are unwrapped while modern generated messages retain their concrete type, and cover a registered v1-only detail in a round trip test.
findings.title: Unwrap legacy status details before returning them
findings.why_it_matters: Callers decoding a status detail generated by the original protobuf generator now receive an internal v2 wrapper instead of their registered concrete message, so existing type switches and assertions fail. Previously ptypes.DynamicAny converted the resolved message through MessageV1 and returned the original type. Converting the result with protoadapt.MessageV1Of restores that behavior while retaining v2-generated concrete messages.
